name: Goi cuon
summary: Gỏi cuốn, on Vietnam Tourism’s local-eating page, is a fresh roll of green lettuce and herbs around rice noodles, steamed pork, and a single prawn, with a thick fermented dipping sauce. Vietnam Tourism’s national dish list also sets a roll in Hanoi and describes rice paper, leafy greens, mint, coriander, a protein, and a garlic chive, with hoisin or nước chấm.
origin: The local-eating page remembers the roll as an after-school snack in this city and as a break at any hour. The photograph is the roll. The file does not name a city.
culture: Vietnam Tourism says you sit on a plastic stool and eat the rolls as a snack, with iced tea after a walk.
texture: The page says the dipping sauce is thick and fermented, and that the sauce is the part that makes the difference.
howToEat: Green lettuce and herbs around rice noodles, steamed pork, and one prawn. The sauce is the part the page tells you to notice.
The door it names is Gỏi cuốn Minh, 84/33 Bùi Viện, District 1. Street vendors around the city are the other place it gives.
where: Street vendors around the city, and Gỏi cuốn Minh at 84/33 Bùi Viện. No shop clock was printed.
In Hanoi, Vietnam Tourism’s national dish list names Quán Ăn Ngon at 18 Phan Bội Châu, Hoàn Kiếm. The hour is Check on arrival.
seoTitle: Gỏi cuốn in Ho Chi Minh City
seoDescription: Fresh rolls as Vietnam Tourism describes them in Ho Chi Minh City: lettuce, herbs, noodles, pork, one prawn, and a thick fermented sauce.
